version.changelog:
**Major update: Adds multi-level difficulty, flexible question count, diverse question types, and progress tracking.**

- Introduced three difficulty levels: junior, mid, and senior, with intelligent inference from resume or user prompt.
- Allows flexible question counts (supports 5, 10, 15, 20, or custom) based on user request.
- Standardizes five question types: knowledge, coding, system design, case study, and behavioral.
- Tracks interview history and progress, including capability radar analysis.
- Supports both document (markdown) generation mode and interactive mock interview mode.
- Significantly enhanced natural language intent/difficulty/quantity detection in both Chinese and English.
- Added support for progress prompts such as "历史记录", "进步", and interview practice tracking.

vt.analysis:
Type: OpenClaw Skill
Name: ai-interview-coach
Version: 3.0.0

The 'ai-interview-coach' skill bundle is a comprehensive tool designed to assist users with interview preparation. It analyzes resumes (PDF, Word, Markdown) and generates tailored interview questions across various difficulty levels and roles. The skill includes instructions for the AI agent to maintain a local history file at '~/.ai-interview-coach/history.json' to track user progress and generate capability radar charts. All identified behaviors, including file reading and local persistence, are explicitly documented and directly support the stated functionality. No evidence of data exfiltration, malicious execution, or unauthorized system access was found in SKILL.md or the supporting documentation.

llm.summary: This is an instruction-only interview-prep skill whose stated behavior matches its instructions: it reads user-provided resumes/role descriptions, generates questions, and (optionally) records session history — there are no unexplained credentials, installs, or network endpoints.

dimensions.detail: Name/description (interview question generation, resume analysis, mock interviews, history) match the SKILL.md content. The skill only asks for inputs relevant to that purpose (resume files, job role text, user difficulty/count preferences).
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: Instructions explicitly tell the agent to read user-supplied files (Markdown, PDF, DOCX) and extract resume content, infer difficulty, generate questions, and format output. This is within scope. The doc mentions using a “PDF tool” but does not name one; it also describes saving history and session files (e.g., ~/.ai-interview-coach), which implies filesystem writes — reasonable for this skill but worth noting because it will read files you point it to and may write local history files.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: No install spec and no code files — instruction-only. That minimizes risk from downloaded code or package installs.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: No required environment variables, credentials, or external endpoints are requested. The declared requirements are proportionate to the described functionality.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: always:false and autonomous invocation allowed (platform default). The README/SKILL.md describe saving history under ~/.ai-interview-coach and session files; the manifest did not declare config paths, but local storage of user-provided session data is coherent with the feature. Users should expect the skill to write/read user-specified resume files and history files on disk.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance: This skill appears coherent and self-contained. Before using it: 1) Be aware it will read any resume file path you provide — don't point it at files with secrets or unrelated private data. 2) It may write history/session files to ~/.ai-interview-coach (per README); check that directory and delete or move files if you prefer not to keep local history. 3) The SKILL.md mentions using a PDF extraction tool but doesn't specify which — if your platform requires explicit permission to access files or run extraction tools, grant it only if you trust the environment. 4) No external API keys or credentials are requested. If you see prompts later asking for network credentials or unrelated secrets, decline and investigate further.
